title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n10 = 1, n01 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report preregistration, execution accounting (201 model calls: 200 shared initial + 1 repair), paired analysis, failure diagnosis, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are proposed as tools to translate operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational safety in such workflows depends on produced configurations satisfying deterministic invariants (reachability, policy compliance, loop‑freedom, and ordered-change/workflow constraints). Prior prototype work on intent→configuration and the literature advocating verifier-integrated generator pipelines motivate empirical measurement of how verifier-based guardrails change end-to-end correctness [1],[2].

This study asks a narrow, preregistered question: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate→validate→repair, ≤1 repair) reduce deterministic-invariant violations relative to single-shot generation? The design isolates the marginal effect of an automated verifier-triggered repair (not effects of alternative prompts, constrained generation, or independent multi-sample strategies). We executed the preregistered paired design (CAND-2026-001) with 200 deterministic tasks, a deterministic verifier, and the hosted model gpt-5-mini; all artifacts and accounting are archived.
sections.related_work:
Recent NetOps studies examine intent→configuration translation and prototype evaluation pipelines but generally vary in task scope, device coverage, and verification integration [1],[2],[3]. Cross-domain work on generate→validate→repair in program-repair and tool-augmented agent architectures shows the practical value of external oracles for reducing incorrect or unsafe outputs [4],[5]. Surveys of agentic AI and LLM safety emphasize documented failure modes (hallucination/confabulation) and recommend verifier stages and provenance recording for operational workflows [6],[7].

Our contribution situates a tightly controlled verifier-centered empirical test—grounded in a preregistered estimand and archived execution—within that literature. Unlike multi-model benchmark rankings, we quantify a single, well-specified estimand: the paired difference in deterministic-verifier acceptance between a single-shot baseline and the same shared initial candidate after permitting one guarded repair invocation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered (CAND-2026-001) before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — binary per-task outcome whether the deterministic verifier accepted the generated configuration (all encoded invariants pass). The preregistration fixed sampling, generation semantics, failure-treatment rules, and the single confirmatory test.

Sampling and task bank: We used deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 to produce 200 intent→configuration tasks focused on very_hard and extreme workflow patterns (difficult multi-device ordering constraints, dependency rules, and staged rollouts). Sampling indices and inclusion/exclusion rules were fixed in the preregistration; no preregistered exclusions occurred. Each task includes an explicit required_sequence, expected_final_state, and allowed-touched-fields encoded in the task manifest; representative task manifests and responses are archived.

Generation semantics and model configuration: The preregistered generation_semantics value was shared_initial_candidate: for each task the adapter made exactly one initial model generation that was deterministically reused by both the baseline and guarded episodes. Independent first-pass generations per condition were not produced. The declared model was gpt-5-mini and the archived execution model_configuration.json records temperature = null (unset). We explicitly note that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0; nondeterministic hosted-model sampling remains possible. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter orchestrated model calls, deterministic validation, and at-most-one repair per task as specified in the preregistration.

Verifier and scoring rules: We used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 to compute the binary outcome. The verifier performs: (1) deterministic syntactic parsing, (2) per-device allowed-field checks, (3) encoded workflow/ordering constraints (the required_sequence per task), and (4) network-level invariants (e.g., at-least-one-up group constraints). The verifier's decision rules are deterministic and archived together with validator traces for each episode. Per-task outcome is "all invariants pass" (score = 1) or "any invariant fails" (score = 0).

Execution accounting and failure rules: The adapter allowed a single automated repair call only if the verifier flagged failures for the shared initial candidate. Missingness and unparsable outputs were handled per preregistration: the automatic_syntax_sanitizer_v1 attempted deterministic fixes; persistent unparsables after sanitizer and the permitted repair were logged as persistent unparsable and treated per the prespecified sensitivity analysis. The sampling plan specified a paired design (N = 200 pairs) and maximum_model_calls = 400; the stopping rule required both episodes for all preregistered tasks or exhaustion of the model call budget.
sections.results:
Execution summary and accounting: The run executed to completion between 2026-09-01T16:03:05.491039+00:00 and 2026-09-01T16:32:13.298536+00:00 (start and completion recorded in the execution manifest). Planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared initial generations + 1 repair call). The deterministic reconciliation artifact and provider audit record these stage counts.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: Baseline accepted by verifier in 199/200 tasks (baseline_success_rate = 0.995). Guarded accepted in 200/200 tasks (guarded_success_rate = 1.000). Contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered confirmatory test used an exact two-sided McNemar implementation appropriate for small discordant counts; that exact implementation enumerates the binomial distribution of discordant-pair outcomes to compute the two-sided p-value given (n10,n01). For our observed discordant counts (n10=1,n01=0) the exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0. We supplement the discrete inference with a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference = [0.00, 0.015] computed with 10,000 resamples and seed 1729 (bootstrap parameters are archived).

Repair activity and diagnosis: The guarded pipeline invoked a single repair for one task; that repair changed the single failing baseline into a guarded success. The archived validator trace for that pair shows the failure was a multi-step ordering/workflow violation against the task's required_sequence (an ordering breach across interfaces). The repair produced a corrected sequence that satisfied the verifier's encoded invariants and the verifier accepted the repaired candidate. Representative per-task responses and scoring artifacts (execution/responses/ and execution/scoring/) are archived and include the shared initial candidate, final validated configuration, and the validator's before/after traces.

Missingness, exclusions, and deviations: No preregistered exclusions occurred; no persistent unparsables or failed episodes were recorded under the predefined missingness policy. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and that all consistency checks passed. There were no deviations from the preregistration recorded in the analysis artifacts.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation bound by design choices: Because the preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, the baseline and guarded episodes began from the same sampled initial candidate. Therefore the observed paired difference isolates the marginal effect of the verifier-triggered repair (the repair-only effect), and does not measure effects of constrained prompting, distinct guarded-first-pass prompts, or multi-sample model prompting. We state explicitly that independent first-pass contrasts (baseline-first-pass vs guarded-first-pass) would require a different preregistered execution semantics and were not performed here.

Statistical context and realized precision: The preregistration planned power to detect ~10–15 percentage-point paired changes at N = 200 under mid-range baseline assumptions. The observed baseline success rate (99.5%) was much higher than those planning assumptions, so realized power to detect modest absolute improvements was limited. The single repaired case yielded an absolute increase of 0.5 percentage points; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 is a discrete-test consequence of observing only one discordant pair in the n10 direction. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies realized uncertainty: while the data are consistent with a small positive effect, the experiment lacks power to assert generalizable effects beyond this synthetic corpus and single repaired case.

Failure-mode implications: The single repaired failure was a multi-device ordering constraint breach—consistent with our preregistered hypothesis that multi-device policy interactions and ordered workflows are likely concentrated failure modes. The artifact-grounded failure taxonomy in the archived analysis maps the repaired task to an ordering/workflow pattern; this suggests verifier-guarded repair can be effective when failures are localized to reordering or sequence-conformance faults that the repair generator can correct deterministically.

Threats to validity and scope: Internal validity is constrained by the shared-initial semantics and by reliance on one deterministic verifier whose encoded invariants define the pass/fail outcome. Construct validity depends on whether the verifier's encoded invariants adequately capture operational correctness; while our verifier enforces syntactic, per-device, workflow, and some network-level invariants, it does not emulate live-device runtime behaviors or telemetry. External validity is limited: tasks are synthetic, the experiment used one hosted model (gpt-5-mini), and no adversarial contamination or poisoned-retrieval attacks were included. These limitations mean operational generalization to heterogeneous production environments requires further multi-model, live-device, and adversarial evaluations.

Reproducibility and artifact availability: All execution artifacts (task manifest, provider traces, responses, validator traces, analysis tables, and the execution manifest) are archived and indexed in the execution bundle. Key numeric results reported here (counts, contingency table, model_calls_used = 201, bootstrap parameters) exactly match archived analysis files. Researchers seeking to reproduce the analysis can consult the archived execution_manifest that indexes raw_results.jsonl, analysis artifacts, model_configuration.json, and validator traces; these artifacts contain the full machine-verifiable provenance for the run.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation that measured the marginal effect of a verifier-triggered repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics on deterministic invariant compliance for intent→configuration tasks. With gpt-5-mini on a synthetic, deterministic task bank, baseline compliance was 199/200 and guarded compliance was 200/200; a single verifier-triggered repair corrected one workflow-ordering failure. The observed paired risk difference was small (0.005) with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015], and the discrete exact McNemar test reflects the single discordant pair (p = 1.0). The experimental artifacts precisely document execution accounting (200 shared initial generations + 1 repair = 201 model calls), validator traces, and analysis outputs. The principal scientific lesson is constrained: in this artifact-grounded synthetic setting, a verifier gate with a bounded repair corrected a localized ordering fault, but broader operational claims require multi-model evaluation, independent first-pass contrasts when that estimand is of interest, adversarial contamination testing, larger and noisier task banks, and live-device validation.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the manifest indexing archived artifact paths). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock; humans selected the broad topic family and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock as permitted by the track.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent first-pass generation contrasts.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
